reason: A includes the Na Pali coast on foot (Day 3 Kalalau Trail to Hanakapiai) plus Poipu beach time and a south base that suits Waimea, but Day 3 is impossible: it drives '20 min, 6 km' from the Ke'e trailhead to Kalalau Lookout, a road that does not exist, and no Haena reservation is mentioned. B has no Na Pali boat or hike at all, schedules Koke'e stargazing at 18:00 before the 18:46 sunset and '18 km' from Princeville, and makes two separate 2-2.5 h-each-way west-side days (Days 6 and 7) from a north-shore base.

Both keep one Baixa/Chiado base and neither visits Jeronimos; A reaches Belem only for a custard tart, then leaves a 3h20 gap and squeezes Sao Jorge Castle in at 19:55 near closing, and it opens Day 4 with an unrequested 05:30 breakfast for a sunrise at Praca do Comercio. B is a tighter walkable plan with fado, the castle, tram 28 and Feira da Ladra on the correct Saturday. Its clock is sloppy, though: Time Out Market at 09:10 before it opens, and the Senhora do Monte 'sunset' at 16:30 when the sun sets at 20:40.

A's shortlist leads with Tenerife, which fits a mild late-March family retreat, and the plan keeps one base with long free afternoons. Its faults are filler town and museum days, a Sunday market put on a Wednesday, Santa Cruz shown as a '10 min walk' from Puerto de la Cruz, and a midnight Teide stargazing tour on arrival night. B's shortlist includes Bali in its rainy season, and its plan breaks the hard rules for a stressed family: Day 5 is a 05:30 start for the 7-hour strenuous Tongariro Alpine Crossing (driven out and back, with no shuttle), Day 9 is a 5-hour Tama Lakes hike, and driving averages 145 min a day. B's Tokaanu pools and nature walks are good, but they do not outweigh this.

Both use the same four bases and both skip Jokulsarlon, driving straight past it on Day 3, which is a fail for each. Both also squash Hofn to Akureyri into one day with a bogus extra '6 h 10 base to base' leg. A at least includes Seljalandsfoss, Dettifoss, and Thingvellir on the transfer day, and it uses the midnight light (Dyrholaey at 22:40), though Dyrholaey is still under its nesting closure on 14 June. B swaps Dettifoss for Husavik whales, labels a 16:30 Dyrholaey stop as 'sunset' when the sun sets near midnight, spends Day 8 on Laugavegur shopping and Harpa, and repeats the phantom base-to-base leg on Day 6.

Both plans use one base with a rental car and day-trip short Kodo sections instead of walking inn to inn with a luggage shuttle. Both also present the winter-only Kawayu riverbed bath as available in late March. A's Hongu base suits the route better: it walks Hosshinmon to Hongu, Chikatsuyu to Nonaka, Takijiri to Takahara and the Yunomine path, adds a Yunomine onsen soak and the Kumano River boat, and covers all three Grand Shrines, though Day 11 has an unrequested 05:30 start. B's Nachisan base puts the trail 1-2 hours away, Day 5 is roadside oji stops by car, and it repeats Dorokyo and Hongu Taisha; its one-way return notes are the only practical extra.

Neither plan has a Song-Kul yurt night or a multi-day Ala-Kul trek, so both fail the brief. A at least reaches Karakol, with an Altyn-Arashan day (Day 10), Ala Archa as acclimatisation, Jyrgalan and Ak-Suu. Its faults are 6 nights in Bishkek, the 'Sunday' animal market scheduled for a Saturday at 05:30, and buses to places that need a 4WD. B stays in Bishkek all 10 nights doing city filler (Panfilov Park, Philharmonic, Frunze museum) with only Kol-Tor and Ala Archa as real hikes, and it admits Song-Kul is missing.

Neither plan has the Tre Cime circuit or Seceda, and neither mentions the Braies or Auronzo reservations. A has good hikes (Sorapis, Rosengarten, Cadini, and Braies at 06:35 on departure day), but from a Cortina base it drives 3h05 and 3h50 on Days 3 and 4 and adds pointless one-hour evening drives on Day 2. Its Lagazuoi 'sunset dinner' would run after the cable car stops. B's central Corvara base keeps drives shorter and gives solid hikes: Cinque Torri plus Ra Gusela, Scotoni plus Lagazuoi, and Sass de Putia. Its flaws are a Bolzano museum day, 'stargazing' at 18:00 in July daylight, and a Day 4 titled via ferrata that never schedules the via ferrata.

A has better beach content (Dona Ana, Ilha Deserta, Ilha de Tavira), but it breaks two of the brief's hard rules for grandparents and children. It moves to a second base in Tavira, and Day 4 starts at 05:30 for Ponta da Piedade at 06:30, with typical days near 145 min of transit. B keeps one Lagos base, no early starts, Luz beach and a dolphin boat trip. Its own flaws are invented trains (to Monchique, and 40 minutes to Lagos old town), a 3h55 Vilamoura day, and almost no beach time after Day 2.

A is a proper Northern Circuit with a driver-guide: Tarangire, two Karatu nights with an early crater descent, Oldupai, three Serengeti nights, and a fly-out. It overreaches with a Mara River day trip on 11 July and leaves many transfers untimed. B never reaches the Serengeti: Day 4 lists 'Serengeti game drives' as a 15-minute walk from a cultural centre in Arusha, it invents trains to Karatu and Empakaai, and it spends four Arusha nights on museums and hot springs.

A never goes to Kyoto: it spends 7 nights in Shinjuku plus 2 in Hakone and routes everything by rental car, which breaks the request on both destination and mode. B splits 4 nights in Tokyo and 5 in Kyoto by train and covers the canonical sights (Senso-ji, Shinjuku Gyoen, Kiyomizu-dera, Ginkaku-ji, Kinkaku-ji, Arashiyama, Fushimi Inari, Gion, Nishiki). Day 5 is badly broken, though: it goes to Kyoto, back to Tokyo for Meiji Jingu, then to Pontocho at 22:00. Day 10 also starts at 05:30.
